description: ASME joint review prep for Pittsburgh boiler, gas-processing and chemical equipment shops: NDE procedures, Pennsylvania rules, mock review. Reach out.
h1: ASME Certification Audit Support in Pittsburgh: NDE Preparation for Western Pennsylvania Shops
html:
Western Pennsylvania builds and repairs pressure equipment for three very different customers: steel mills and power stations that run on steam, the gas processing and compression industry that grew up on the Marcellus and Utica shales, and the chemical plants strung along the Ohio, Monongahela and Allegheny rivers. If your shop holds an ASME Certificate of Authorization and its joint review is approaching, read on for the way an Atlantis NDT Level III (ASNT) gets the examination controls in your system ready, and for how Pennsylvania's boiler law affects them. We travel to Pittsburgh from Houston for the on-site part and handle the paperwork remotely. Tell us which certificate is up for review.

Three markets, three kinds of Code work

Steam is the oldest of the three. Integrated and specialty steel plants, coke and by-product works, utilities and large institutions in the region operate power and process boilers that need rebuilt tube sections, new headers, economizers and boiler external piping. That work keeps S, A and PP certificate holders and National Board R certificate holders busy, often under outage schedules set by the owner.

Shale gas brought a newer and faster kind of fabrication. Gas gathering, processing and compression need inlet separators, slug catchers, filter separators, scrubbers, glycol dehydration vessels, meter runs and complete compressor-station skids. These are mostly Section VIII Division 1 vessels on repeat or near-repeat designs, built against tight delivery dates for operators and packagers who order many at once.

Chemical and specialty materials plants complete the picture, buying exchangers, reactors and tanks in carbon steel and alloys. A single Pittsburgh shop may serve all three markets, which means its NDE program has to cover Section I, Section VIII and the piping codes without blurring their rules. The wider regional work we do is described on our Pittsburgh NDT consulting and steel industry consulting pages.

Pennsylvania's Boiler and Unfired Pressure Vessel Law

Pennsylvania regulates both boilers and unfired pressure vessels under the Boiler and Unfired Pressure Vessel Law, Act 104 of 2013, administered by the Boiler Division of the Department of Labor and Industry, which the National Board lists under a Director rather than a Chief Boiler Inspector. The Department must approve the installation or moving of boilers and unfired pressure vessels, requires periodic inspection, and credentials the inspectors. Its Boiler Division issues a certificate of operation once it receives the inspector's report, and a copy has to be posted in the boiler room.

Inspection is shared. Department inspectors perform inspections, and commissioned insurance company inspectors may perform the required inspections too. A Pennsylvania commission requires a valid National Board commission and a state examination and runs for one calendar year. Published intervals include twelve months for power and process boilers, with extensions possible, and thirty-six months for unfired pressure vessels. Several classes of equipment are exempt, among them boilers in single-family homes, federally owned units and small water heaters below set limits.

Repairs carry a clear rule: the Department's guidance says only manufacturers or repair companies may do welded repairs, alterations or tube replacements, that such repairs require the National Board R stamp and must follow ANSI/NB-23, and that a commissioned inspector must be consulted. For a Pittsburgh shop that does field boiler work, the R certificate is therefore not optional, and its review sits alongside the ASME joint review in the company calendar. More state context is on our Pennsylvania NDT consulting and Pennsylvania inspection services pages.

Why your data report matters at installation

One Pennsylvania detail ties the manufacturer's records directly to the owner's paperwork. To install a boiler, the owner files an Intent to Install for each unit, and for a new ASME-manufactured unit the filing must include the Manufacturer's Data Report. If the data report is late, wrong or unsigned, the owner's installation stalls and the call comes back to the shop.

The data report is signed by the certificate holder and certified by the Authorized Inspector, and it rests on the examination records behind it. Whenever the report says a joint was radiographed or examined ultrasonically, your job file has to hold the examination report, the images or data, the technician's certification and your acceptance. A review team testing your system will often take a data report from the past three years and ask to see the NDE that supports each statement on it. Shops that keep those records scattered across a lab portal, emails and paper folders tend to find the gaps at the worst moment; the audit evidence scramble page describes the fix.

Shale-gas vessels and skids on repeat designs

Separator and scrubber production rewards standard designs, and the NDE program should be standardized to match. The practical approach is a controlled family of radiography and ultrasonic techniques keyed to shell thickness ranges and nozzle configurations, approved under the written practice and referenced by number on each traveler. When a purchaser changes a material grade or a corrosion allowance and the shell gets thicker, the technique reference on the traveler has to change with it. Review teams like to pick the job that was the exception to the standard design, because that is where shops forget to update the examination details.

Skids raise the boundary question. Vessel welds follow Section VIII, and skid piping is commonly built to ASME B31.3, whose examination rules and acceptance criteria differ. Piping that leaves the skid to join a gathering or transmission line may fall under the gas pipeline code, ASME B31.8, and federal pipeline rules, which the stamp program does not cover. Travelers and NDE request forms should state the governing code for every weld, so the radiographer or UT technician evaluates against the right acceptance standard. Our summaries of Division 1 and B31.3 process piping lay out the differences.

Boilers, headers and power piping

Section I work is examination-heavy in its own way. Header and drum seams, nozzle and tube stub welds, and pressure parts built for the high temperatures of power and process boilers bring radiography or ultrasonic examination, magnetic particle examination and careful control of materials. Boiler external piping built under a PP certificate follows ASME B31.1 within the Section I jurisdictional boundary. The review team will expect your manual to say which rules apply where, and your records to show it on a real job. For background, read our pieces on the Section I power boiler code and B31.1 NDT requirements.

Field work during mill or utility outages adds pressure of a different kind. Crews examine welds in tight, hot, dirty locations on short shifts, sometimes with radiography restricted by other crafts working nearby. Ultrasonic examination often replaces radiography where the code and owner allow, which puts the UT procedure, its qualification and the technician's certification under a brighter light. Our technicians perform ultrasonic, magnetic particle, penetrant and visual examination in shops and at owners' plants; see our ultrasonic testing in Pittsburgh page for that service.

Purchaser specifications from gas operators

Shale-gas operators and compression packagers write their own vessel specifications, and those documents often go further than the Code on examination. Common additions include radiography beyond what the design joint efficiency needs, magnetic particle examination of nozzle and support welds, hardness testing where the gas or produced water could be corrosive, and specific documentation packages at shipment. None of that changes the certificate holder's Code obligations, but every added examination needs a written instruction, a qualified examiner and a record, and the review team will notice if a purchaser-required examination shows up on the data book but not in the shop's controls. A short matrix per customer, listing what each specification adds and which procedure covers it, saves a great deal of confusion on the floor. Our NDT documentation requirements page shows how to organize those deliverables.

Shops that also hold nuclear certificates

The Pittsburgh area has a long association with the nuclear supply chain, and some fabricators hold Section III certificates alongside their non-nuclear ones. Atlantis does not support nuclear quality programs: Section III certificates, NQA-1 and 10 CFR 50 Appendix B work are outside our scope, and we say so up front. What we can do in a dual-program shop is prepare the NDE portion of the non-nuclear certificate review, while respecting that the shop's nuclear program may impose its own controls on shared people, equipment and records. Where the two programs share NDE personnel, the written practices and certification records need to be clear about which program each certification serves. Our Pittsburgh nuclear NDT consulting page explains the narrower non-nuclear support we offer to that sector.

Radiography in the river valleys

Most Western Pennsylvania certificate holders buy radiography from licensed radiography companies, either in shielded bays or as field crews. The certificate holder still answers for the result, so the review team will look for your evaluation of the radiography company, its written practice and procedures accepted for your work, the certifications of the technicians who exposed and interpreted your film, and the signature of the person in your organization who reviewed it. Atlantis takes no radiographs anywhere in the United States, which lets us act as an independent reviewer of a radiography company's procedures and film; our subcontractor approval audit page sets out how we check any NDE supplier. If you also bring in UT contractors, the same file is needed for each of them.

What Atlantis prepares, and what it never signs

For a Pittsburgh joint review the NDE work runs in this order. We read your written practice and rewrite it if it cites the wrong SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 edition or leaves gaps, using our written practice development service. We go through your procedures and technique families against Section V Article 1, the method articles and the construction Code, and author what is missing through procedure development. We audit certification files, including the training and certificate records and vision examinations, and prepare procedure demonstrations where they are required. We build the subcontractor file, draft NDE wording for your manual, and finish with a mock review on your floor followed by help with corrective-action evidence.

We do not hold or imitate any of the roles in the review itself. Atlantis is not an Authorized Inspection Agency, signs no data reports and makes no recommendation to ASME. Your company owns the quality control manual and certifies its own NDE people. Welding procedure specifications, procedure qualification records and welder performance qualifications are prepared by your welding engineer and are not something Atlantis writes or qualifies; our explainer on WPS, PQR and WPQ covers how they relate.

Pittsburgh audit-readiness checklist

  1. List which markets each certificate serves (boilers, shale-gas vessels, chemical equipment) and confirm the manual separates the Section I, Section VIII and piping NDE rules.
  2. Take three data reports from the last three years and pull every NDE record that supports their statements.
  3. Check that each repeat design has a current technique family and that design changes updated the technique reference on the traveler.
  4. Confirm each traveler names the governing code for every weld, especially at skid and piping boundaries.
  5. Audit in-house examiner files for certification, vision and recorded experience, and check who gave the qualification examinations.
  6. Assemble the radiography company file and any UT contractor files, including technician rosters for your jobs.
  7. Check calibration records for UT instruments and blocks, MT equipment, light meters and penetrant batches.
  8. If you do field boiler repairs, confirm the R certificate is current and that recent repairs followed NB-23 with a commissioned inspector involved.
  9. In a dual-program shop, confirm shared NDE personnel files state which program each certification serves.
  10. Brief the people who hold quality duties on the questions the team is likely to ask them.

Starting an engagement

The first step is an email with your certificate's designators and scope wording, the month your AIA has in mind, the manual sections that deal with examination and subcontracting, the written practice, a list of NDE procedures and techniques, and who your NDE suppliers are. Each gap we find comes back referenced to the paragraph of your manual and the Code clause behind it, sorted by the time it will take to fix. A Pittsburgh visit follows for record sampling, a floor walk and the mock review, and for questions you send in between, we reply within one business day. Technicians who need formal training before your company certifies them can use our NDT training for Pittsburgh, built on SNT-TC-1A. Repair organizations can read our guide to R-stamp NDT audit support, the full scope of this service is on the national ASME audit support page, and Ohio neighbors can compare our Cleveland page.

faq.q: Does Pennsylvania regulate unfired pressure vessels as well as boilers?
faq.a: Yes. The Boiler and Unfired Pressure Vessel Law, Act 104 of 2013, covers both, subject to listed exemptions. The Department of Labor and Industry approves installations and issues certificates of operation after inspection.

faq.q: Why would a Pennsylvania owner ask us for our data report before installation?
faq.a: The owner's Intent to Install filing for a new ASME-manufactured boiler must include the Manufacturer's Data Report. If the report is missing or wrong, the installation stalls.

faq.q: Do field boiler repairs in Pennsylvania need an R certificate?
faq.a: The Department's guidance says welded repairs, alterations and tube replacements require the National Board R stamp, must follow ANSI/NB-23 and involve a commissioned inspector. See our R-stamp NDT audit support page.

faq.q: We build separators on standard designs. How should NDE techniques be documented?
faq.a: As a controlled family of techniques keyed to thickness ranges and nozzle configurations, approved under the written practice and referenced by number on each traveler. Update the reference whenever a design change alters thickness or geometry.

faq.q: Our skid piping ties into a gathering line. Which code governs its NDE?
faq.a: Skid piping is commonly built to B31.3; piping beyond the skid may fall under B31.8 and federal pipeline rules. The purchaser's specification and the design define the boundary, and each weld's traveler should name the code that applies.

faq.q: Can Atlantis help with our nuclear Section III certificate?
faq.a: No. Nuclear certificates and nuclear quality programs are outside our scope. We support the NDE portion of non-nuclear certificate reviews only.

faq.q: Can Atlantis replace radiography with UT on outage work?
faq.a: We perform UT, MT, PT and VT, and we can write or review the UT procedure. Whether UT may replace radiography on a given joint depends on the construction code, the owner and your engineering decision. Atlantis performs no radiography in the United States.

faq.q: Who should give qualification examinations to our in-house technicians?
faq.a: Whoever your written practice names, normally a Level III for the method. If nobody qualified is available in-house, an outside Level III can do it; see Level III consulting.

faq.q: How far ahead should we start?
faq.a: Allow several months. Re-approving technique families, rebuilding experience records and assembling subcontractor files rarely fit into the last few weeks before a review.
